title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, and Runbooks (Standards and Templates)
author: Ari Chen
summary: Standards, concrete examples, and templates for defining SLOs and error budgets, performing capacity planning, running reliability initiatives, executing incident reviews, and authoring operational runbooks across Redwood Inference services.
content:
## Purpose
This document defines the SRE standards and operational playbooks for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review requirements, operational tooling expectations, and runbook templates used by Redwood Inference. It is intended for service owners, SREs, on-call engineers, and product stakeholders.

## Scope
Applies to all production-facing services including, but not limited to: Redwood API (hosted inference), Inference Runtime (serving runtime), Dedicated routing service, Authentication/Authorization, Embeddings pipeline, and Observability ingestion.

## Ownership
- Document owner: eng-sre
- Primary contacts: SRE on-call rotation (pager duty), Service owners in product/engineering
- Review cadence: annual review or after any major incident affecting SLOs

---

## SLO & Error Budget Standards
### Principles
- SLOs must reflect customer-facing user experience (availability, latency, correctness where applicable).
- Keep SLOs simple and measurable. Avoid overly brittle metrics.
- Every SLO must be linked to its indicator, objective, measurement window, and owner.

### Required metadata for every SLO (as page fields)
- Service name (string)
- SLI (metric expression) e.g., `success_rate(http_5xx == 0 AND latency_ms < 500)`
- Objective (percentage, e.g., 99.95%)
- Measurement window (rolling 30d / 7d as required)
- Error budget (1 - objective)
- Primary owner (team/person)
- Alerting thresholds and burn policy actions

### Example SLOs (templates)
1) Redwood API (text generation endpoints)
| Indicator | Objective | Window | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Availability (request success & 5xx rate) | 99.95% | 30d | Success = 2xx/1xx w/o service 5xx |
| Latency (p95 end-to-end) | p95 < 300ms | 30d | Measured at edge after auth |

2) Inference Runtime (per-cluster inference service)
| Indicator | Objective | Window | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Model inference success (no OOM, complete token stream) | 99.9% | 30d | Important for long-context models |
| Token-generation latency (p90) | p90 < 40ms/token | 30d | Depends on model & hardware |

3) Embeddings Pipeline
| Indicator | Objective | Window | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Ingest to embed completion | 99.99% | 30d | Critical for search freshness |
| Batch job latency (p95) | p95 < 5m | 7d | Bulk loads only |

---

## Error Budget & Burn Policy (Standard)
Error budgets are used to balance reliability investments against feature velocity. The following tiers define required actions as a function of error budget burn over a rolling 7-day window unless otherwise noted.

- Green (burn < 25% of 7d budget): Normal operations. Teams may proceed with planned releases.
- Yellow (25% <= burn < 50%): Notify stakeholders, recommend delaying non-critical releases, increase monitoring frequency.
- Orange (50% <= burn < 75%): Mandatory release freeze for customer-impacting changes, schedule focused reliability work, prepare rollback/playbooks.
- Red (burn >= 75%): Escalate to engineering leadership, require a mitigation plan within 4 business hours, implement temporary mitigations (traffic shaping, capacity increase, fallback model), postpone all feature deployments until budget is restored.

Actions must be documented in the SLO page and in the service runbook. When red-level burn occurs, a short incident-style pager (low-impact) may be opened to coordinate mitigation.

---

## Capacity Planning Standards
### Objectives
- Ensure predictable headroom for steady-state and burst traffic.
- Define thresholds and runbook actions for scaling, pre-warming, and decommissioning.

### Key metrics and definitions
- Provisioned capacity: resources allocated to a service (GPU count, replica count, vCPU, memory).
- Utilization: rolling average of resource consumption (target metrics: CPU/GPU utilization, inflight requests per replica).
- Safe headroom: target spare capacity kept to absorb traffic spikes (default 20% for user-facing inference clusters).
- Scale margin: buffer used for autoscaler setpoints (default 30% above target utilization).

### Capacity planning process (quarterly)
1) Traffic and trend analysis: 90/95/99 percentiles for request rates and tokens/sec by endpoint.
2) Tail-event analysis: identify peak-day and burst patterns (hourly/day-of-week).
3) Model profiling: compute expected per-request resource cost for commonly used models (tokens per request, KV-cache hit rate impact, quantization profile).
4) Plan sizing: translate expected Q growth into forecasted resource requirements and cost.
5) Runbooks & rehearsals: schedule game-days for pre-warm and scaling rehearsals.
6) Capacity purchase/commit: engage finance for Dedicated capacity purchases 30–60 days ahead of forecasted need.

### Example calculation (simplified)
- Expected peak qps: 2,000 requests/s
- Average tokens per request: 25 tokens
- Average tokens/sec per GPU (profiled): 100,000 tokens/s
- Required GPUs = ceil((2,000 * 25) / 100,000) = ceil(0.5) = 1 GPU; apply safe headroom 20% => 2 GPUs recommended for redundancy and headroom.

---

## Reliability Initiatives (RIs)
### Initiative types
- Preventative: dependency upgrades, capacity hardening, stateful-system resilience work.
- Observability: add SLIs, dashboards, tracers, and synthetic traffic.
- Recovery: improve workflows that shorten time-to-recover (TTR) such as automated rollback, warm standby.

### Lifecycle
1) Proposal: short PRD with success metrics (expected reduction in P50/P95 incidents or error budget burn).
2) Pilot: deploy to canary environment and measure impact.
3) Rollout: staged rollout with observability hooks.
4) Review: post-rollout measurement against objectives and update SLO documentation if needed.

---

## Incident Review & Postmortem Standards
### Mandatory contents for every postmortem
- Summary and impact (customers, severity, duration)
- Timeline with timestamps (detection -> mitigation -> resolution)
- Root cause analysis (causal chain and contributing factors)
- Actions and owners (PRs, runbook changes, monitoring additions) with ETA for completion
- Error budget impact calculation and follow-up (does this change SLOs?)

### Review process
1) Draft postmortem within 72 hours of incident resolution.
2) Internal review with SRE, service owner, and at least one engineering peer within 7 days.
3) Publish in Confluence and link to the SLO page.
4) Track action items in Jira with owners and deadlines; SRE manager validates closure.

### RCA standards
- Use the 5-Whys and causal factor charting.
- Distinguish between root cause and contributing factors.
- Estimate probability and detectability for each contributing factor and propose mitigation that reduces either probability or improves detection.

---

## Operational Tooling Expectations
Required baseline tooling for all production services:
- Metrics: Prometheus for SLI collection (or equivalent), aggregated into long-term metrics store (e.g., Cortex/Thanos).
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry traces collected and sampled to representative percentage; traces linked to traces UI with sample URLs in incidents.
- Logging: Structured logs shipped to central store (Elastic/Cloud provider) with retention policy per confidentiality classification.
- Alerting: PagerDuty integration with severity-based routing; alert rules documented in SLO pages.
- Canary & synthetic traffic: scheduled synthetics for core flows; failures count towards an SLO alert if they correlate to user impact.
- Capacity & costing dashboards: show provisioned vs used, projection, and cost per token/request.

Recommended integrations and automation:
- Automatic error budget burn calculations and dashboarding.
- Playbook triggering from alert burn thresholds.
- Automated scaling policies with manual override and pre-warm APIs for inference clusters.

---

## Runbook Template (required per critical service)
Paste this template into every service runbook and keep it up to date.

1) Service Overview
- Purpose: short description of what the service does.
- SLOs: link to SLO page(s) and numeric objectives.
- Owners: primary and secondary on-call, pager, slack channel.

2) Health Indicators
- Primary SLIs and dashboards (links)
- Key logs and error signatures to search for

3) Alerting & Initial Triage
- Typical pager(s) that may fire and what they mean
- Quick triage checklist (5 bullets):
  - Is the service reachable (DNS/ LB)?
  - Are backend dependencies healthy?
  - Is there an ongoing deployment?
  - Check error budget burn dashboard
  - If latency spike: check queue/backpressure and GPU/memory saturation

4) Mitigation Steps (ordered by speed-to-impact)
- Short-term: restart affected pods/instances, enable degraded mode, route traffic to fallback models, increase replicas.
- Medium-term: scale cluster, increase capacity reservation, revert deploy.
- Long-term: schedule postmortem, implement automated recovery steps.

5) Escalation Matrix
- L1 on-call -> L2 SRE -> Service owner -> Eng manager -> Director on-call (contact list and phone/pager IDs)

6) Runbook Maintenance
- Last updated, owner, change log entries.

---

## Runbook Example (short)
Service: inference-runtime-us-east-1
- SLO: 99.9% inference success, p90 token latency < 40ms
- Pager: inference-runtime-high-errors
- Quick mitigation: disable model X fallback (if misbehaving), scale inference replicas by +2, set traffic to secondary region using routing policy.

---

## Documentation & Publishing Requirements
- Every SLO and runbook must be published in Confluence under eng-sre and linked from product/service docs.
- Changes that affect customer SLAs or SLOs require notification to growth/support and an update to the pricing/legal pages.
- All postmortems and reliability initiative outcomes must link back to SLO pages and associated runbooks.

## Compliance & Audit Notes
- Keep a change log of SLO/objective changes for audit (who, when, why).
- For regulated customers, attach the confidentiality label `restricted` on service pages where data residency or retention differs.
